content:
support-bot: ALERT: customer Monarch (ticket M-4212) reporting p99 generation latency ~2.1s (baseline ~800ms). Spike started ~2026-03-15T18:34Z. Region: us-west-2. Model: rw-13b-v1-q4. Ticket: https://redwood/support/M-4212

kai: ack. Is Monarch on Hosted or Dedicated? any recent deploys? pinging runtime oncall.

support-bot: Monarch is on Hosted (prod region us-west-2). No auto-scheduled maintenance. Last change: routing policy update yesterday.

lisa: I can run a quick perf test with their tenant token on a staging copy of traffic. Need token scope from SRE. @nina can you hand off?

ben: any deploy activity in the last 24h? I saw a config push for kernel selector two days ago.

omar: noted — we saw tail spikes after kernel-selector tweak in canaries last week. Would like a pprof/data capture on affected nodes + KV cache hit rates. PromQL I usually run: `sum(rate(runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant=\"monarch\"}[5m])) by (le)` and `sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{tenant=\"monarch\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{tenant=\"monarch\"}[5m]))`

nina: copying LB logs now. early glance shows a handful of requests routed to fallback variant (rw-13b-v1-q4-slim) at ~18:33Z which would increase latency due to smaller-context decoding. attaching snippet: `LB: route -> variant=rw-13b-v1-q4-slim node=us-west-2-12`

kai: plan: 1) @lisa run perf bench on a replay of 1000 requests (prod-like load) 2) @omar collect profiles + cache metrics 3) @ben audit routing change + recent deploys 4) @nina collect LB traces. Sync in 30m. Owner: @lisa (lead). :thumbsup:

lisa: running bench now (using bench/run_latencies.sh --tenant monarch --replay 1k). quick paste of running output:

```
requests: 1000
p50: 120ms
p90: 480ms
p99: 1.92s
mean seq_len sampled: 640
notes: p99 correlates with seq_len > 512
```

omar: grabbing pprof from nodes that handled the slow traces. Early sign: high memcpy time inside attention kernel on NVRM driver v520.x nodes. Also seeing increased single-request batches (batch_size=1) on those nodes.

ben: I pulled git history: routing policy change `ae3f9b2` pushed yesterday (resource-based fallback thresholds lowered). That explains more fallbacks into the slim variant. Not a code deploy but config change.

sara: FYI Monarch's SLO is 1s p99 for interactive generation. Customer PM asked for ETA.

kai: immediate mitigations: 1) raise fallback threshold to reduce routing to slim variant, 2) schedule canary rollback of kernel-selector tweak if profiling confirms kernel regression. @deploy-bot prepare rollback window.

deploy-bot: canary rollback scheduled: runtime kernel-selector rollback to release v1.81.9 at 1901234700 UTC. Will run canary on 5% of traffic then ramp if green.

lisa: after forcing routing to prefer main variant we see p99 drop to ~980ms on the bench replay (single run). Will let bench finish full run and post final numbers.

omar: pprof full: majority time in attention memcpy + a small codepath in kernel selector that picks scalar fallback for small batches on these nodes. I can prepare a revert patch for the selector change (commit a1b2c3d -> revert).

ben: I'll open a small config change PR to bump fallback threshold back to previous value and coordinate with @sre for a quick rollout.

kai: ETA update for customer: aiming for canary rollback + routing tweak to be validated within ~2 hours. I'll update ticket M-4212.

support-bot: ticket M-4212 updated: engineering on it, planned mitigations = routing tweak + canary rollback, ETA ~2h. Customer notified.

sara: thanks team. once canary is green we should run a regression test matrix for seq_len distribution >512 and confirm no throughput regressions.

lisa: bench finished: final p99 940ms, p95 420ms. uploading artifacts to S3: s3://redwood/diag/monarch/1901234567/bench.tar.gz

omar: pushed revert PR for kernel-selector (PR #4982) — requesting review from @ben @lisa.

kai: great. stay on this until rollback validated. we'll reconvene for postmortem tomorrow. :eyes:
